article_content: Oscar-nominated actress Emily Mortimer has shared intimate reflections on navigating motherhood alongside her acting career. Balancing acclaimed roles like MacKenzie McHale in HBO’s *The Newsroom* with caring for her children Samuel (10) and May (4) has created profound internal conflict. 'Leaving home for work carries a lingering guilt,' Mortimer told *The Observer Magazine*, acknowledging how her film commitments often require 14-hour days. Despite contributing financially to her family with husband Alessandro Nivola, she questions whether society undervalues caregiving roles. 'I wish my daughter could pursue her dreams without doubting her choices,' she remarked. These insights resonate amid ongoing conversations about working parents’ challenges, following Gwyneth Paltrow’s polarizing remarks on the entertainment industry’s unique parenting difficulties.

article_content: A long-awaited report on the national curriculum has raised concerns about teachers' poor grammar and punctuation. The federal government released the 288-page report by former teacher and Liberal staffer Kevin Donnelly and business professor Ken Wiltshire on Sunday. It recommended a de-cluttered, parent-friendly and back-to-basics approach. Excessive content was found to affect students' learning quality, particularly in primary schools, while literacy and numeracy skills—including phonics—needed prioritization. The report urged schools to return to basics, emphasizing foundational skills like reading, writing, counting, critical thinking, and understanding Australian identity. Prime Minister Tony Abbott believes this approach will boost economic outcomes and student employability, though critics argue it may neglect 21st-century competencies. Education Minister Christopher Pyne supported adopting most recommendations, calling the review non-ideological. The report criticized demonization of Western civilization and Judeo-Christian heritage in curricula. Key proposals included greater flexibility, improved accessibility for special needs students, and restructuring the curriculum authority as a private entity. Critics like Greens Senator Penny Wright accused the review of sidelining Indigenous perspectives, while Queensland Premier Campbell Newman stressed the need for well-rounded democratic citizenship education. The government will finalize its response in early 2015 following state consultations.

article_content: A Super Puma helicopter transporting 19 oil workers executed a controlled emergency landing 14 miles west of Fair Isle in the North Sea. Aberdeen Coastguard reported the October 22 incident involved a scheduled crew change flight. Three rescue choppers and RNLI lifeboats from Kirkwall, Aith, and Lerwick responded, recovering all personnel safely though their health statuses remain undisclosed. Operator CHC Helicopters confirmed their incident protocols were activated. This follows a May 2012 survival incident involving 14 passengers, contrasting with the fatal 2009 crash that killed 16 near the BP Miller platform.

article_content: 'Severely distressed': U.S. student Melody Davis (20) died two weeks after suffering respiratory failure in a hospital car park. Staff directed her companions to call 999 rather than offering immediate aid. Davis, studying English Literature at the University of Liverpool, collapsed from acute asthma-induced hypoxic brain injury. Friends Grace Kelly and Elizabeth Port attempted to seek help at Royal Liverpool University Hospital's reception but were instructed to dial emergency services. The decision to drive her instead of waiting for paramedics was later deemed unwise by coroner Andre Rebello, though no institutional fault was assigned. The hospital updated its on-site emergency protocols following the tragedy.

article_content: Arjen Robben has expressed joy at rejoining the Netherlands squad following a period of enforced absence during recent international matches, during which he openly vented frustration while watching from home. The winger, who last represented the Oranje at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil before injuries sidelined him for two games—against Italy and the Czech Republic—stated his eagerness to contribute positively. 'It’s great to be back and I aim to make amends,' he remarked ahead of crucial Euro 2016 qualifiers against Kazakhstan and Iceland. Robben described his distress after the narrow loss to the Czechs, admitting he yelled so intensely at home that his wife reminded him the children were asleep. He emphasized the squad's need to secure victories in both upcoming matches, noting 'we must win twice after falling behind early.' Meanwhile, Robben continues strong form with Bayern Munich, netting three goals this season.
